Sample CTV Ads for Punctual Pros

The ad plan names two CTV spots for the first test, "Storm Ready" (:15) and "We Watch the Clock" (:30, cut to :15). Both sell the on-time guarantees the three franchise brands already make (Punctual Pros ad plan). The finished scripts are not in the context, so the outlines below are working drafts built only on those guarantee lines.

The two test spots

SpotLengthCore messageBrand line used
Storm Ready:15Know who to call before the furnace failsOne Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
We Watch the Clock:30, cut to :15Punctuality as the productBen Franklin $5-a-minute guarantee; Mister Sparky "America's On-Time Electrician"

Draft: "Storm Ready" (:15)

  • 0–5s: Winter evening. A thermostat display, then a cold house.
  • 5–11s: A One Hour truck pulls up. On-screen text shows the guarantee line.
  • 11–15s: End card with the brand, a unique tracking number and a QR code.
  • The aim is familiarity before the emergency, not an instant call (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Draft: "We Watch the Clock" (:15 cut)

  • 0–5s: Close-up of a wristwatch, then a technician at the door.
  • 5–12s: Three quick beats, one per brand, each with its own guarantee line.
  • 12–15s: Punctual Pros end card with a tracking number and QR code.
  • The :30 version gives each brand longer on screen. Do not add claims beyond the existing guarantees.

Production specs

  • Lengths of :15 and :30. Resolution 1920x1080 preferred, 16:9, H.264 or ProRes (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Loudness of -24 LKFS ±2 dB. Some platforms quote -23 LUFS.
  • Frequency cap of 3 per week, checked in week 3.

How the spots are judged

  • The two spots split 50/50 by zip cluster in week 2. About 15% of Tier-I zips are held out (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Success means cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift. Completion rate does not count, because it runs about 94–99% by design.
  • In the week-4 read, 20% of CTV budget shifts to the winning cut.
  • The $12 cost per site visit is an assumption and must be replaced by the week-8 read (est.).

Gaps in the data

  • No storyboards, voiceover copy or seasonal variants are in the context. The creative brief or agency files would show them.
  • No home-services CTV benchmark for cost per lead exists in the plan's sources.

Next actions

  1. Get the final scripts and storyboards for both spots from the creative owner. Check every claim against the three brand guarantees.
  2. Assign a unique tracking number, UTM and QR code to each cut in ServiceTitan before the week-2 launch.
  3. Confirm with franchisor marketing that the brand lines and end cards meet brand standards.
  4. Have the deliverables checked against platform specs (loudness, resolution) before the week-1 deadline.

# Sample CTV Ads for Punctual Pros

The ad plan names two CTV spots for the first test, **"Storm Ready" (:15)** and **"We Watch the Clock" (:30, cut to :15)**. Both sell the on-time guarantees the three franchise brands already make (Punctual Pros ad plan). The finished scripts are not in the context, so the outlines below are working drafts built only on those guarantee lines.

## The two test spots

| Spot | Length | Core message | Brand line used |
|---|---|---|---|
| Storm Ready | :15 | Know who to call before the furnace fails | One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!" |
| We Watch the Clock | :30, cut to :15 | Punctuality as the product | Ben Franklin $5-a-minute guarantee; Mister Sparky "America's On-Time Electrician" |

## Draft: "Storm Ready" (:15)
- **0–5s:** Winter evening. A thermostat display, then a cold house.
- **5–11s:** A One Hour truck pulls up. On-screen text shows the guarantee line.
- **11–15s:** End card with the brand, a unique tracking number and a QR code.
- The aim is familiarity before the emergency, not an instant call (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## Draft: "We Watch the Clock" (:15 cut)
- **0–5s:** Close-up of a wristwatch, then a technician at the door.
- **5–12s:** Three quick beats, one per brand, each with its own guarantee line.
- **12–15s:** Punctual Pros end card with a tracking number and QR code.
- The :30 version gives each brand longer on screen. Do not add claims beyond the existing guarantees.

## Production specs
- Lengths of :15 and :30. Resolution 1920x1080 preferred, 16:9, H.264 or ProRes (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Loudness of -24 LKFS ±2 dB. Some platforms quote -23 LUFS.
- Frequency cap of 3 per week, checked in week 3.

## How the spots are judged
- The two spots split 50/50 by zip cluster in week 2. About 15% of Tier-I zips are held out (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Success means cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift. Completion rate does not count, because it runs about 94–99% by design.
- In the week-4 read, 20% of CTV budget shifts to the winning cut.
- The $12 cost per site visit is an assumption and must be replaced by the week-8 read (est.).

## Gaps in the data
- No storyboards, voiceover copy or seasonal variants are in the context. The creative brief or agency files would show them.
- No home-services CTV benchmark for cost per lead exists in the plan's sources.

## Next actions
1. Get the final scripts and storyboards for both spots from the creative owner. Check every claim against the three brand guarantees.
2. Assign a unique tracking number, UTM and QR code to each cut in ServiceTitan before the week-2 launch.
3. Confirm with franchisor marketing that the brand lines and end cards meet brand standards.
4. Have the deliverables checked against platform specs (loudness, resolution) before the week-1 deadline.
